subject: Billing footprint and partial-token rounding for BrightCart pilot
messages:
From: Alyssa Carter <alyssa@brightcart.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-12-11T09:14:00Z
Subject: Quick question on billing footprint for pilot

Hi Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re mapping out the pilot for BrightCart’s itemization assistant and I need a tight answer on how billing looks when we mix a lot of short streaming calls with occasional long-context summarization (30k token extraction). Specific asks: 
- Are very short streaming calls (single-turn suggestions, ~15–40 tokens generated) rounded up to a minimum quantum? If so, is that quantum per-API-call or per-session?
- When we do a long-context batch call that uses the full 30k context, how do we account for prefix reuse/kv cache credits across subsequent calls?
- Any sample invoice line item you can share for mixed usage?

We’re especially sensitive to surprises in month 1 of the pilot — can you confirm what an expected worst-case unit billing would look like for ~200k streaming tokens + 1x 30k long run?

Appreciate any examples. If easier, we can hop on a 20-min call.

Best,
Alyssa
Head of Product — BrightCart
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Carter <alyssa@brightcart.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-12-11T11:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick question on billing footprint for pilot

Thanks, Alyssa — good questions. I pulled together a short note and a sample line-item (attached pricing_deck_v2.pdf) so you have concrete numbers. High level answers below; attached has the worked example.

1) Minimum / quantum for short streaming calls
- For the BrightCart pilot we typically apply a lightweight quantum to streaming-only microcalls to avoid a large number of sub-token charges. Our pilot standard is: streaming microcalls are rounded up to the nearest 8-token quantum per request.
- Important: that 8-token quantum applies per API call (i.e., each separate streaming request) unless the calls are made within the same session identifier within a 5-minute active window — in that case we aggregate and bill on the aggregated token count before rounding.

2) Long-context runs and KV reuse
- Long-context calls (where you provide a 30k context) are billed per-token consumed for the given request; we do not apply the 8-token quantum to long-context requests.
- If subsequent calls reuse the same prefix within the same conversation/session and the KV cache hits are present, we issue a prefix-reuse credit that reduces billable tokens on the follow-up call. Credits are applied at invoice time and shown as a separate line item ("KV reuse credit").

3) Mixed-usage interaction (how we bucket)
- We bucket by conversation/session id over the billing day. Any streaming microcalls that fall into the same conversation and within the 5-minute active window are summed before we apply the 8-token rounding. Long-context runs are billed as their own line item. Example in the attached deck shows exactly how ~200k streaming + 1x30k long-run breaks down.

Pilot concession (we can do this as a one-time credit):
- For month 1 of the pilot we can waive the 8-token quantum so streaming microcalls are billed per-token (no rounding) — this avoids surprise overhead at the start. After month 1 we revert to standard quantum unless we agree otherwise.

If that sounds reasonable I’ll loop in legal for a brief amendment to the SOW. Would you like us to waive the quantum for the entire pilot instead of just month 1?

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
From: procurement@brightcart.com
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-12-12T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick question on billing footprint for pilot

Marissa / Karthik —

Thanks for the quick note. A couple clarifications before we sign anything: 
1) Is the 8-token quantum ever applied retroactively to calls that were aggregated across a day? For example, if we have 5 separate streaming calls across an hour that are outside the 5-minute aggregation window, do they each round separately?
2) Will the prefix-reuse credit show up as a negative invoice line, or is it an internal adjustment? We need something that maps cleanly to our GL.

Also attached are contract redlines (redlines_contract.docx). We’d like the month-1 quantum waiver formalized in the SOW and, if possible, request that Redwood consider a pilot discount on token rates (we suggested 10% in the doc). Can you confirm if there’s flexibility?

Cheers,
BrightCart Procurement Team
procurement@brightcart.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-12-12T12:20:00Z
Subject: INTERNAL: negotiation plan for BrightCart (pilot) — please weigh in

Folks —

Summary of ask from BrightCart: 
- Clarify per-call vs aggregated rounding behavior (they want assurance no surprise rounding across day)
- Formalize month-1 waiver of the 8-token quantum in SOW
- Request 10% pilot rate discount on token unit price
- They've provided redlines to the contract (attached to external thread)

Recommendation: 
- Confirm that rounding is per-call unless calls are within the 5-minute active window assigned to same session id; we should also offer to show them the invoice sample lines and an end-of-month reconciliation export for transparency. That should address GL concerns.
- Approve month-1 waiver (no rounding for streaming microcalls). This is low-cost and high-trust.
- Tradeoff: offer a one-time pilot credit equivalent to a 15% discount on committed volume if they sign a 3-month pilot (committed min). This preserves margin and gives them a perceived larger concession than 10%.

If legal is comfortable with a short amendment, I’ll send the revised SOW and the DocuSign link. Karthik — can you confirm the margin math and whether 15% on the committed slab is okay? Stephanie — if finance is good with the pilot credit flow, I’ll route the amendment.

Thanks,
Marissa
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Carter <alyssa@brightcart.com>, procurement@brightcart.com, contracts@brightcart.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-12-13T16:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick question on billing footprint for pilot — confirmation and next steps

Hi Alyssa —

Great to sync on this. Confirming the outcomes below so we’re all aligned: 

1) Rounding and aggregation
- Standard policy: streaming microcalls are rounded up to the nearest 8-token quantum per API call. Aggregation: if multiple streaming calls share the same session id and occur within a 5-minute active window we sum tokens before applying rounding.
- We will provide a sample invoice export for your GL team that shows line-by-line items and any KV reuse credits (those appear as negative line items labeled "KV reuse credit").

2) Pilot concessions (agreed)
- Month 1: 8-token quantum waived for all streaming microcalls so you will be billed per-token (no rounding).
- Commercial: we can offer a pilot credit equal to 15% of committed volume if you sign up for a 3-month pilot minimum (details in the SOW). If you prefer the straight 10% token-rate discount we can accept that too — I included both options in the amendment.

3) Next steps
- I’ll ask legal to prepare a short SOW amendment that includes the month-1 waiver and the pilot credit option. I’ll send a DocuSign link when ready.
- Once the amendment is signed, we’ll schedule a technical onboarding call and a short invoice-template walkthrough (suggested time: Tuesday 2025-12-16, 11:00am PT).

Attachments: pilot-sow.pdf (summary of pilot terms we’ll put in the amendment).

If that captures everything, please indicate preference on the commercial (15% credit on 3-month commit vs 10% flat discount) and we’ll route the amendment.

Best,
